oewn-05925333-n.learner: an idea you are not sure about but still partly believe.
examples: once or twice pleased herself with the notion that, as he looked at her, he was trying to trace a resemblance
While these newly-born notions were passing in their heads, the perturbation of Elizabeth's feelings was every moment increasing.

oewn-05844922-n.learner: a broad idea that takes in many things.
examples: That is his notion of Christian forgiveness!

oewn-05928143-n.learner: an idea that is strange, made up in the mind, or taken up on a sudden fancy.
examples: he was struck with the notion of doing a very gallant thing, and called out to her

connotation.why: treats the idea as a passing fancy rather than a real thought

oewn-02498011-v.learner: to fill someone's time in a way that is pleasant and enjoyable.
examples: Elizabeth took up some needlework, and was sufficiently amused in attending to what passed between Darcy and his companion.
wishes were vain; or, at best, could serve only to amuse her in the hurry and confusion of the following hour
His silly faces amused the children until they laughed out loud.

oewn-07435271-n.learner: harm or loss that falls on someone, or something given up.
examples: indulged their mirth for some time at the expense of their dear friend's vulgar relations
the young man's marrying her was a patched-up business, at the expense of your father and uncle

oewn-13296518-n.learner: money paid out for goods and services, of a kind that can often be taken off a tax bill for this year rather than counted as the cost of lasting property.
examples: The shop listed rent, wages and postage as expenses for the year.

oewn-13298909-n.learner: money you spend to do your job, which your employer usually pays back to you.
examples: She kept every receipt so the company would repay her travel expenses.
He is a pleasant fellow, and would jilt you creditably.
"He is as fine a fellow," said Mr. Bennet, "as ever I saw.

oewn-09955448-n.learner: someone who belongs to the same group or line of work as you.
examples: He sent the news round to his fellow doctors.

oewn-09965384-n.learner: a friend who is often in your company.
examples: He was her constant fellow, walking out with her every day.

oewn-00747485-v.learner: to ask for something to be brought or supplied to you.
examples: I hope, my dear, that you have ordered a good dinner to-day
Kitty, run down and order the carriage.

oewn-00748704-v.learner: to tell someone to do something, speaking with the power to make them do it.
examples: The captain ordered the men to stay below deck.

oewn-00749139-v.learner: to give a command that something be done.
examples: The judge ordered a new trial.

oewn-00869308-v.learner: to give a reason or explanation that shows why something is so.
examples: though a day seldom passed in which Elizabeth did not account for it clearly, there seemed little chance of her ever considering it with less perplexity

oewn-02613467-v.learner: to be the only or the main thing behind how something exists, is got, is supplied, or is got rid of.
examples: Two farms account for nearly all the milk sold in this town.

oewn-00967067-v.learner: to tell or describe something in words.
examples: She accounted the events of that night to the court.

oewn-02516039-v.learner: to make something weaker or milder, or to hold it back and keep it within limits.
examples: If you, my dear father, will not take the trouble of checking her exuberant spirits
Elizabeth had frequently united with Jane in an endeavour to check the imprudence of Catherine and Lydia

oewn-00663742-v.learner: to look at something closely to see whether it is right, good, or in working order.
examples: He checked the brakes before driving down the hill.

oewn-00922307-v.learner: to find something out for certain, usually by asking or by taking some trouble over it.
examples: She checked what time the shop closed before setting out.
she observed him looking at her earnestly
Most earnestly did she then entreat him to lose no more time before he wrote.

oewn-13999199-n.learner: a disorderly state that comes about when people do not act in the way you would expect.
examples: My mother was taken ill immediately, and the whole house in such confusion!
While the family were in this confusion, Charlotte Lucas came to spend the day with them.

oewn-07523151-n.learner: a feeling of embarrassment that leaves your mind unclear.
examples: a question which she could not answer without confusion
years of happiness could not make Jane or herself amends for moments of such painful confusion

oewn-05691387-n.learner: a state of mind in which your thoughts and behaviour are not clear or orderly.
examples: The fever left him in such confusion that he could not name the day.

oewn-00787849-n.learner: serious and careful work meant to do or achieve something.
examples: Elizabeth had frequently united with Jane in an endeavour to check the imprudence of Catherine and Lydia

oewn-00798547-n.learner: a piece of work taken on with a purpose and worked at hard, especially one that needs effort or courage.
examples: The voyage across the ice was a bold endeavour, and few expected them to return.
